subject: Opt-in reconciliation & dedupe plan for Glow Expo badge scans
messages:
From: Elena Marquez <elena@glowexpo.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Hughes <tom@eventtech.io>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:14:00-05:00
Subject: Question: badge-scan opt-in flags and duplicates

Hi Kim —

Thanks again for the Redwood demo at Glow Expo. After the show our ops team pulled the badge-scan export and we ran into two problems we need help with before ingesting into HubSpot:

1) Duplicate scanner hits: multiple badge scans per attendee (scan devices at session doors and sponsor booths) generated ~7.5k rows where a single person can have 3–6 scan rows.
2) Opt-in ambiguity: some entries have the opt-in flag set, others show blank; our onsite form had a single checkbox but some devices failed to persist the state. We need guidance on a safe reconciliation approach that preserves consent and minimizes CRM duplication.

I've attached the raw_scans_export.csv so you can see the fields. Can Redwood run a reconciliation pipeline that:
- groups on email + normalized phone OR badge ID heuristics,
- applies a conservative opt-in merge (prefer explicit "yes" anywhere, never flip a recorded "no" to yes), and
- exports intended HubSpot updates plus a short exception report for manual review?

We also might need a short updated consent language to append to records that lack a timestamped opt-in. Can your team share a suggested copy we can display in follow-ups?

Would like to schedule a quick call tomorrow to align.

—Elena
Elena Marquez
VP, Events & Sponsorships
Glow Expo

Attachment: raw_scans_export.csv (csv, 7.8 MB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Marquez <elena@glowexpo.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-18T10:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Question: badge-scan opt-in flags and duplicates

Elena —

Thanks for the export and the clear ask. We can absolutely run a reconciliation and produce: a) a staging CSV with a single resolved contact per attendee, b) a HubSpot import template with mapped properties, and c) an exceptions file for anything that requires manual verification. High-level plan below — please confirm and we'll kick off a dry-run on staging.

Proposed plan (conservative defaults):
- Identity resolution: primary key = email (when present); fallback = phone_normalized + last_name + first_name; badge_id used as supporting evidence but not sole dedupe key.
- Opt-in merge rules: if any record for that resolved identity has explicit opt-in = TRUE with timestamp, set opt-in = TRUE. If any record has explicit opt-out = TRUE, preserve opt-out (never flip to opt-in). If all are blank, flag in exceptions.
- Conflict handling: if multiple explicit emails map to same phone + name, include both in exceptions for manual mapping.
- HubSpot mapping: we will map: first_name, last_name, email, phone, company, job_title, opt_in_source, opt_in_timestamp, original_scan_ids (concatenated).

Attachments I will circulate: consent_text_v3.docx — suggested copy for follow-up (short, explicit, includes mail and SMS language); dedupe_rules.xlsx — the threshold criteria we propose for auto-merge.

Questions for you:
1) For blank opt-ins, do you prefer us to set a property "consent_confirm_needed = true" and leave follow-up to your campaign team, or do you want Redwood to add a soft-opt-in email (one-time) asking for confirmation before marking HubSpot property?
2) Any PII redaction rules we should apply (e.g., strip badge_id after 90 days)?

If you agree to the plan, we'll schedule a 1-hour alignment call (I can do tomorrow 11/18 3pm ET or 11/19 10am ET). Also, I see the DPA addendum in your doc — please send the DocuSign link if you want us to sign before processing.

Best,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
